input.objectiveText: Explain what the equal sign means using the balance scale example
input.intent: Engage students with a live tutor asking spoken-response questions that prompt them to say aloud what '=' means ('same as' or 'balanced') when looking at various scale images.

data.title: Balance and the Equal Sign
data.description: You will answer out loud to explain what the equal sign means.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Four plus one equals five. What does the equal sign mean in this equation?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing stating that the two sides match, weigh the same, or are equal counts.
items.signatureError: Saying the sum, five, or reading the numbers back is NOT an explanation.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Four plus one is the same as five.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Three equals three. What does the equal sign tell us here?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing stating that the two sides match, weigh the same, or are equal counts.
items.signatureError: Just repeating the number three or saying it is a counting word is NOT an explanation.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Three is the same as three on both sides.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Two plus three equals one plus four. What does the equal sign mean when we see this?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing stating that the two sides match, weigh the same, or are equal counts.
items.signatureError: Saying that the equal sign just means the answer comes next is NOT correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Two plus three balances with one plus four.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Six equals four plus two. Why is the equal sign used between these two parts?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing stating that the two sides match, weigh the same, or are equal counts.
items.signatureError: Saying the final answer, six, without explaining the sign is NOT correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Six is the same amount as four plus two.

input.objectiveText: Explain the secret rule behind a repeating or growing pattern
input.intent: Have the tutor show a simple pattern (such as 2, 4, 6, 8 or red-blue-red-blue) and let students say the rule aloud into the microphone (e.g., 'plus two' or 'red then blue').

data.title: Pattern Rules
data.description: Practice explaining pattern rules out loud!

items.conceptStatement: This pattern alternates between red and blue.
items.ask: Look at the colors: red, blue, red, blue. What is the repeating rule?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing that names the correct alternating color order counts as the rule.
items.signatureError: Naming just one color or saying the last color is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The pattern goes red then blue over and over. Say red then blue.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding two each time.
items.ask: Listen to the numbers: two, four, six, eight. What is the growing rule?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that describe adding two or counting by twos count as the rule.
items.signatureError: Saying the next number ten is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The numbers grow by adding two each time. The rule is plus two.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern alternates between a square and a circle.
items.ask: Look at the shapes: square, circle, square, circle. What is the repeating rule?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing that names the correct alternating shape order counts as the rule.
items.signatureError: Naming only one shape is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The shapes repeat in order as square then circle.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding five each time.
items.ask: Listen to the numbers: five, ten, fifteen, twenty. What is the growing rule?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that describe adding five or counting by fives count as the rule.
items.signatureError: Saying the next number twenty-five is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The numbers grow by adding five each step. The rule is plus five.

items.correctionBody: The rule is square then circle because those shapes repeat in that order.
